query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a titanium diboride (TiB2) coating on boride-based components will improve their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion by forming a stable, protective interfacial layer that resists chemical attack and minimizes aluminum infiltration.
generation.material_initial_state: Boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, without any additional protective coatings.
generation.intervention: Application of a titanium diboride (TiB2) coating to the surface of the boride-based components.
generation.conditions: Exposure to molten aluminum at typical operating temperatures (e.g., 660–750°C) and under conditions of continuous contact with the molten metal.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable TiB2 interfacial layer that resists chemical reactions with molten aluminum and prevents aluminum infiltration into the substrate.
generation.mechanism: TiB2 has high chemical stability and low solubility in molten aluminum, which allows it to act as a barrier against aluminum attack. This reduces the rate of material degradation by preventing direct contact between the molten aluminum and the underlying boride-based substrate.
generation.predicted_outcome: The TiB2-coated components will exhibit significantly lower mass loss and surface degradation compared to uncoated boride-based components when exposed to molten aluminum under identical conditions.
generation.baseline: Uncoated boride-based components exposed to molten aluminum under the same conditions.
generation.boundary: The improvement in corrosion resistance is expected to hold as long as the TiB2 coating remains intact and adherent to the substrate. Mechanical damage to the coating or exposure to temperatures exceeding the stability range of TiB2 may reduce its effectiveness.
generation.uncertainty: The extent of improvement in corrosion resistance depends on the quality and thickness of the TiB2 coating, as well as the specific composition of the boride-based substrate and the molten aluminum alloy.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of boride-based components: one set with a TiB2 coating and one set without any coating. Expose both sets to molten aluminum at 700°C for 100 hours. Measure mass loss, surface morphology, and chemical composition of the exposed surfaces.
measurements: Surface morphology using scanning electron microscopy (SEM)
Chemical composition of the surface using energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the TiB2-coated components exhibit similar or greater mass loss and surface degradation compared to the uncoated components, the hypothesis will be falsified.
